cuts.raw_narration: A close-up profile of Hisoka, the tall pink-haired man in a jester-like outfit, standing in a sunlit forest with a subtle smirk on his face. He is speaking to Gon, whom he has just defeated. Hisoka tells Gon he has decided to let him live for now, until Gon someday becomes worthy of killing. He returns the badge to Gon, saying he will take it back only when Gon can punch him in the face like Gon just tried. In the meantime, Gon is to hold onto it for him. A high-angle wide shot then shows Gon, a young boy in a green outfit with an orange backpack, sprinting away across a barren sandy clearing, kicking up a trail of dust behind him — visibly rattled after the humiliating encounter.

In a misty forest, three older thug hunters — a large muscular man in a yellow-and-black striped baseball shirt with a blue cap, one in an orange beanie and dark red turtleneck, and a third in a light-blue shirt and green cap — corner Killua, the small boy with spiky white hair holding his yellow skateboard. The man in the green cap sneers and tells the kid to hand over the badge and he won't get hurt. Killua calmly calls him an idiot. Suddenly Killua appears right behind the hunter in the orange beanie; his fingers have transformed into long sharp claw-like nails, resting near the man's neck. The hunter's face freezes in pure terror — dilated eyes, gritted teeth, sweat pouring down his face under harsh purple lighting. Killua wears a serene, curious look. A moment later two of the brothers stand together in the forest with dark diagonal scratch marks under their eyes, smirking, seemingly unaware that their brother has just been dropped. Killua flips a small oval badge marked 198 into the air, smiling confidently.

Kurapika, the blonde boy in the blue-and-red tabard, sits on the sandy forest floor with Gon standing beside him in his green outfit and Leorio kneeling in his white shirt and glasses next to his red-patterned suitcase. Kurapika lays out a plan: Ponzu, their target, is known for chemical weapons, so Gon can try to track her by the scent of her chemicals. He raises an index finger as he explains. Gon agrees to give it a shot. In an extreme wide shot the three of them stand together dwarfed by the massive roots of a colossal tree as they finalize their strategy. Then a low-angle close-up of Gon against a bright blue sky — his fishing rod propped over his shoulder, wearing a warm, determined smile.

Outside a dark cave entrance in a reddish-lit forest, Gon and Kurapika wait for Leorio, who has gone in alone to find Ponzu. Kurapika, tense, notes that Leorio's thirty minutes are almost up. Gon and Kurapika run into the rocky cave down a sloping stone path, Gon holding his fishing rod, Kurapika carrying his satchel and Leorio's briefcase. Inside, a split shot: severed pieces of a snake lie bleeding on the sandy cave floor while Kurapika stares in shock, a bead of sweat on his face. They find Leorio collapsed and covered in snake bites — an extreme close-up shows his face drenched in sweat, teeth gritted in agony behind his round sunglasses, a bandage on his cheek. Gon frantically tries to help while Kurapika, grim, notes the snakes are venomous vipers and there are far too many bites.
